title: Capacity sourcing mix and price-flex simulator
content:
Executive summary:
This workbook-style doc explores a 3-way capacity sourcing mix (hosted reserved, cloud spot/ondemand, private/on-prem) combined with hiring tranches and price elasticity to estimate unit economics per 1M tokens and monthly burn under different attrition/hiring scenarios. Purpose: give GTM and Eng leads a quick simulator for tradeoffs when committing to Dedicated pools vs relying on elastic cloud.

Assumptions (editable inputs):
- Baseline token volume growth: 20% MoM (scenario A), 35% MoM (scenario B), 10% MoM (conservative)
- Average tokens per request 800
- Hosted reserved unit cost (effective after commit): $0.015 per 1k tokens
- Cloud on-demand unit cost: $0.045 per 1k tokens
- Spot/evictable blended cost: $0.025 per 1k tokens (with 12% failure fallbacks)
- Private infra fully loaded marginal cost: $0.009 per 1k tokens (but includes fixed ops: $120k/mo amortized)
- Hiring tranche: junior engineer fully loaded $18k/mo, senior $28k/mo, platform engineer $35k/mo
- Time to hire per tranche: 10 weeks (fast) / 18 weeks (slow)
- Attrition: 12% annual (base), stress 22%
- QoS penalty/SLAs: fallback to on-demand for spot failures adds 40% extra token cost for failed fraction

Quick reference table (per-1M tokens):
Source | base unit cost (per 1k) | effective cost per 1M tokens | comments
Hosted reserved | $0.015 | $15.00 | assumes minimum utilization 70% of committed
Cloud on-demand | $0.045 | $45.00 | no commitment, higher tail latency cost not accounted
Spot blended | $0.025 | $25.00 | includes fallback penalty for 12% evictions -> +$4.80 per 1M
Private (amortized) | $0.009 + fixed | $9.00 + $120k/mo | economics improve at scale > 20M tokens/mo

Scenario matrix outputs (selected rows):
Scenario: High growth (35% MoM) with fast hiring (10w) and medium attrition
- Month 3 volume: ~12.1M tokens/day -> monthly tokens ~360M
- Recommended mix: 60% hosted reserved, 25% spot, 15% on-demand -> blended cost ~ $18k per 1M tokens equivalent scaled result -> monthly cost ~ $6.48M (note: includes commit amortization)

Scenario: Conservative (10% MoM), slow hiring (18w), high attrition
- Month 3 volume: ~6.6M tokens/day -> monthly tokens ~198M
- Recommended mix: 40% hosted reserved, 40% spot, 20% on-demand -> blended cost ~ $26 per 1M tokens -> monthly cost ~ $5.15M

Headcount tranche plan (sample):
Tranche 1 (Q2): 2 platform eng, 1 ops, 1 SRE -> incremental $99k/mo fully loaded
Tranche 2 (Q3): 3 serving-runtime eng, 2 infra ops -> incremental $162k/mo
Hiring sensitivity: each tranche delayed by 6 weeks increases cloud on-demand spend by ~12% over the period due to lack of reserved pool capacity and more fallback to on-demand.

Break-even analysis:
- For volumes < 10M tokens/mo, private infra never recovers fixed ops vs hosted reserved unless committed utilization > 90%
- For volumes > 60M tokens/mo and predictable growth, private + reserved mix yields >30% lower marginal cost vs on-demand
- Price sensitivity: 10% decrease in end-customer price results in demand uplift ~18% (internal elasticity calibrated from previous GTM experiments). Lowering price too far without capacity commitments pushes unit cost up due to on-demand reliance.

Risks and guardrails:
- Over-commitment to reserved pools if growth stalls -> stranded commit costs; include 6-month step-down clauses in contracts where possible
- Spot dependency increases operational complexity and SRE load; add a 0.5 FTE SRE per 200M tokens/month if spot >30%
- Attrition spikes erode the benefit of private infra due to slower time-to-value for infra ownership

Recommended next steps:
1) Run sensitivity runs with actual feature token mixes (chat vs embeddings vs reranking) — attach per-feature multipliers.
2) Finance to provision a 6-month reserve window for one pilot dedicated cluster sized for 50M tokens/mo as an experiment.
3) GTM to model a staged price promotion tied to capacity commits to test elasticity without jeopardizing margins.
4) Eng-sre to provide failure-mode cost report for spot eviction rates by cloud provider by end of Q2.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working-sheet. Numbers are model outputs, not board-level commitments. Tables above are simplified snapshots; the canonical spreadsheet lives in the linked Confluence and will be updated with actual billing export and hiring pipeline statuses.
